newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota to spend $9 bln on transportation.
newsitem.headline: Bogota to spend $9 bln on transportation.

text.p: Mayor Antanas Mockus has signed a $9 billion agreement with a team of Japanese experts aimed at clearing Bogota of its monster traffic jams.

But the agreement that Mockus signed Monday with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) involves a plan that will take the next 25 years to carry out -- and Mockus conceded in remarks to reporters after the signing ceremony that the city government doesn't have the money to pay for it.

The JICA plan envisages 67 specific road and highway construction projects and the upgrading of the city's notoriously poor public transportation network to help meet the needs of a population that is expected to nearly double in size over the next 25 years.

Mockus noted that the number of cars in Bogota is expected to multiply by 170 percent during the same timeframe, highlighting the need for new roads in the city, where very few have been built over the past 25 years.

Mockus said he would call on the central government to help pay for the project. But he stressed that it will require contributions from all residents of the capital and said taxes would necessarily be going up to ensure that Bogota will be liveable 25 years from now.
